title: A Failover for an Additional Drug is not dispensed, and a new prescription is obtained
rule_summary: DPH Circular DCP 19-12-108, the Electronic Prescribing and Dispensing Manual, states that a Failover results when a prescriber issues an electronic prescription for a schedule VI controlled substance and that electronic prescription is converted and transmitted to a pharmacy as a computer-generated facsimile due to a defect in the electronic prescribing system beyond the prescriber's control or awareness, and that the resulting computer-generated facsimile DOES NOT QUALIFY AS AN ELECTRONIC PRESCRIPTION and frequently does not meet the signature requirements of a written prescription because the electronic signature appears encoded. It states that the ePrescribing regulation allows a pharmacist to dispense a Failover as a valid oral prescription if the listed process is followed, the last condition being that THE FAILOVER MUST NOT BE FOR AN ADDITIONAL DRUG, giving gabapentin as the example. IN THE EVENT THAT A PHARMACIST RECEIVES A FAILOVER PRESCRIPTION FOR GABAPENTIN, OR ANY OTHER MEDICATION DESIGNATED AS AN ADDITIONAL DRUG, THE PHARMACIST MAY NOT DISPENSE THE MEDICATION, AND INSTEAD MUST CONTACT THE PRESCRIBER FOR A NEW WRITTEN OR ORAL PRESCRIPTION. NO ADDITIONAL WRITTEN FOLLOW-UP IS REQUIRED FOR A FAILOVER DISPENSED AS AN ORAL PRESCRIPTION.
exam_relevance: Tests what happens when a Failover does not qualify: the facsimile is not dispensed and the pharmacist contacts the prescriber for a new written or oral prescription, rather than dispensing on the facsimile and waiting for a follow-up prescription.

authority.name: DCP Electronic Prescribing and Dispensing Manual, dispensing schedule VI ePrescriptions and Failovers
authority.section: DCP 19-12-108; Dispensing Schedule VI ePrescriptions - Failovers

exceptions: A Failover dispensed as a valid oral prescription requires no additional written follow-up.
common_confusions: Dispensing on a Failover for an Additional Drug and waiting for a follow-up prescription, when the Manual says the pharmacist may not dispense the medication and must contact the prescriber for a new written or oral prescription.
Reading the no-additional-follow-up statement as a benefit unique to Failovers, when the Manual states that no written follow-up is required for schedule VI oral prescriptions generally.
verification_notes: DPH Circular DCP 19-12-108, the Electronic Prescribing and Dispensing Manual dated 12/27/2019, section on dispensing schedule VI ePrescriptions and Failovers, read in the text published on mass.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
